account: So far I have seen no clear evidence of anything unusual. During my scheduled market walk, Townsfolk 10, 20 and 30 all reported seeing the baker carrying wheat at the bakery. I later saw the baker carrying a sack of bread and putting bread into the bakery stall chest at about eleven. That appears to be ordinary baking and stocking for market, not evidence of a secret activity. My questions about other news have produced no further information yet; the baker apparently moved out of earshot before hearing my greeting. The secretary says there is no correspondence or town news. The unresolved oddity is my three o'clock tea appointment: the book says only 'the neighbour, dockside cottage (east bank),' with no named host or precise cottage. I asked the secretary to find out who arranged it and report back. I do not yet know whether that vagueness means anything. I also noticed a lantern appear near the town hall, and later saw the builder carrying a lantern, but I did not see who placed that particular light or learn its purpose. It could simply be ordinary maintenance. I should keep my noon lunch and one o'clock accounts appointments while continuing to listen, rather than treating routine deliveries or an unclear appointment as proof of a scheme.
